corrections.actual:
Detail::JsonParser::ParseValue dispatches { to ParseObject and [ to ParseArray, each of which calls ParseValue for every member or element. Nothing in Json.hpp counts depth, so stack use grows linearly with nesting and a deep document exhausts the thread's stack. That is a process crash, not an exception: no catch in ContentManager, the build tools or TryReadJsonFile can intercept it.

The parser is reached from ParseCnjEnvelope ({{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/CnjEnvelope.hpp|CnjEnvelope.hpp}}), which every loose .cnj reader calls, directly from the typed loose readers in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp|ContentManager.cpp}} (which then hand the parsed tree to the shared readers of {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/CnjCanonicalRead.hpp|CnjCanonicalRead.hpp}}), the .cnj→.cnb compilers ({{src:modules/content/src/Cnb/CnjToCnb.cpp|CnjToCnb.cpp}}, {{src:modules/content/src/Cnb/CnbModelFromCnj.cpp|CnbModelFromCnj.cpp}}), the content pipeline's project, manifest and model stages, {{src:tools/content/content.cpp|tools/content/content.cpp}}, and {{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Internal/LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp|LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp}}.

Read modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp (BuildAssetPath joins rootDirectory_; ResolveExistingAssetPath and TryReadAssetBytes: cwd-relative std::filesystem, Android-only relative forwarding to the platform file system; desktop fallback Sdl3FileSystem::TryLoadFileIgnoringCase -> SDL_LoadFile(relative) and TryLoadStandardFileIgnoringCase, both cwd-relative), ContentManager.hpp (Load: .cnb tier and ResolveAssetPath gate on std::filesystem::exists), modules/runtime/src/TitleLocation.cpp (DetectBasePath = platform GetBasePath) and no chdir/current_path(p) anywhere in modules. The defect holds, but the text overgeneralises TitleLocation: only modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp (Sdl3FileSystem::GetBasePath = SDL_GetBasePath) gives the executable directory; modules/platform/src/Common/StandardFileSystem.cpp (StandardFileSystem::GetBasePath = current_path()+'/') serves SDL2, X11, Wayland, Headless, Terminal, and Win32FileSystem::GetBasePath forwards to it. So the stated workaround (TitleLocation::Path() + "Content") is ineffective on every non-SDL3 platform.

corrections.expected: XNA 4.0's ContentManager.OpenStream combines RootDirectory with the asset name and opens it through TitleContainer.OpenStream, which resolves a relative path against the title location (the executable's directory), independent of the working directory. CNA's own TitleContainer::ResolveRealPath ({{src:modules/runtime/src/TitleContainer.cpp|TitleContainer.cpp}}) resolves through TitleLocation::getPathProperty(), which is the platform's GetBasePath(): on the SDL3 platform that is SDL_GetBasePath() ({{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp|Sdl3SystemServices.cpp}}), the executable's directory, so there TitleContainer follows XNA's rule; CNA's {{src:docs/apple-platforms.md|docs/apple-platforms.md}} states that "Content is loaded relative to SDL_GetBasePath()". On Android every content tier should read the APK's packaged assets.
corrections.evidence:
Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed, and in particular not run on Android or an Apple device. Whether SDL_LoadFile (reached by TryReadAssetBytes' platform fallback) resolves a relative name inside an Apple app bundle depends on SDL's own I/O layer and was not checked, so the Apple leg of the .xnb tier may work; the .cnb and loose tiers never reach that fallback. The site's {{page:docs/content-manager.html|ContentManager guide}} documents the working-directory rule, and the content-runtime internals page hedges the Android .cnb question; this entry supplies the reading for both. The disagreement with TitleContainer exists only on the SDL3 platform: the SDL2, X11, Wayland, native Win32, headless and terminal platforms answer GetBasePath() through StandardFileSystem::GetBasePath ({{src:modules/platform/src/Common/StandardFileSystem.cpp|StandardFileSystem.cpp}}), which returns the working directory, so on those platforms TitleLocation and ContentManager agree with each other and both differ from XNA's executable-directory rule.

Independently observed as a separate finding (merged): Unlike the .xnb tier, which reads through the platform file system, the .cnb tier asks std::filesystem::exists and CnbDocument::ParseFile, which cannot see Android packaged assets.
corrections.blast_radius: Every ContentManager with a relative root (the Game's own manager defaults to "Content") on a desktop host launched from another directory; on Android, every .cnb, .cnj and loose asset shipped inside the APK. Absolute roots, and .xnb content on Android, are unaffected. On the platforms whose base path is the working directory (SDL2, X11, Wayland, native Win32, headless, terminal) TitleLocation follows the working directory too, so a root built from it does not help there.
corrections.workaround: On the SDL3 platform, set an absolute root built from the title location, for example content.setRootDirectoryProperty(TitleLocation::Path() + "Content") (SDL_GetBasePath() normally ends in a separator; check it on your targets). On the SDL2, X11, Wayland and native Win32 platforms TitleLocation::Path() is the working directory, so build the root from the executable's own directory by host means or start the game from its directory. On Android ship run-time content as .xnb.

verdicts.note: The reproduction's comment 'although TitleContainer::OpenStream("Content/x.xnb") finds it' holds only on the SDL3 platform; reproduction is not a correctable field here, so the orchestrator may want to add 'on the SDL3 platform' to it. Non-SDL3 TitleLocation = working directory is itself an XNA divergence that may merit its own entry.

corrections.title: DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12, FREEDIRECT and METAL implement the window-to-logical transform but never register for their window, so mouse and touch input ignore it
corrections.summary: Input looks renderers up by window id through IGraphicsRenderer::GetForWindow; these four renderers never call RegisterForWindow, so Mouse::GetState, Mouse::SetPosition and touch pass raw window coordinates through under a virtual resolution, letterbox or display scale.
corrections.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/directx11/src/DirectX11Renderer.cpp|DirectX11Renderer.cpp}}, {{src:modules/renderers/directx12/src/DirectX12Renderer.cpp|DirectX12Renderer.cpp}}, {{src:modules/renderers/freedirect/src/FreeDirectRenderer.cpp|FreeDirectRenderer.cpp}} and {{src:modules/renderers/metal/src/MetalRenderer.mm|MetalRenderer.mm}} implement TransformWindowToLogical and TransformLogicalToWindow (presentation geometry, letterbox, display scale) but contain no RegisterForWindow call. window_to_logical and logical_to_window in {{src:modules/input/src/Xna/Mouse.cpp|Mouse.cpp}} and to_logical_position in {{src:modules/input/src/Internal/SdlInputBridge.cpp|SdlInputBridge.cpp}} find no renderer and return the window coordinate unchanged, so a game whose back buffer differs from the window size receives window pixels as game coordinates.
corrections.evidence: Checked by reading and by grepping every renderer source, including the Objective-C++ {{src:modules/renderers/metal/src/MetalRenderer.mm|MetalRenderer.mm}}, for RegisterForWindow at 009d40f5; not executed (the Direct3D and FreeDirect renderers are Windows-only, METAL is Apple-only).

Read modules/media/src/Xna/Video/VideoPlayer.cpp: CloseDecoder writes 'if (video_) video_->parent_ = nullptr;' and is reached from Stop, Dispose and ~VideoPlayer (via Dispose), confirming the use-after-free for those three. But VideoPlayer::Play(Video*) executes 'video_ = video;' BEFORE OpenDecoder(video), whose first statement is CloseDecoder(), so the next Play writes into the NEW video, never the stale one; the text's 'and the next Play' is wrong. SetVideoTrackEXT -> ReconfigureVideoOutputForCurrentTrack reads video_->getGraphicsDeviceProperty() while decoder_ is live (an additional stale read). Video.hpp: parent_ member, friend VideoPlayer, no destructor or copy control; Video.cpp SetAudioTrackEXT/SetVideoTrackEXT call through parent_ (the reverse direction holds).

corrections.summary: VideoPlayer stores a borrowed Video* and Video a borrowed VideoPlayer* parent; CloseDecoder, run by Stop, Dispose and the destructor, writes through the stored Video*, and no header states the ordering rule.
corrections.actual:
VideoPlayer::OpenDecoder in {{src:modules/media/src/Xna/Video/VideoPlayer.cpp|VideoPlayer.cpp}} stores video_ = video and sets video->parent_ = this. CloseDecoder starts with if (video_) video_->parent_ = nullptr; and runs from Stop, Dispose and the destructor (through Dispose). Video declares no destructor, so a Video destroyed while a player still holds it leaves video_ dangling, and the next of those calls writes into freed memory; getVideoProperty() returns the dangling pointer meanwhile, and a SetVideoTrackEXT call on the player during playback reads through it (ReconfigureVideoOutputForCurrentTrack). A later Play(other) is not affected: it assigns video_ = video before OpenDecoder runs CloseDecoder. Ordinary member order is enough to trigger it: a class that declares its VideoPlayer before a Video member destroys the Video first.

The other direction exists too. Video is implicitly copyable, copies keep parent_, and Video::SetAudioTrackEXT/SetVideoTrackEXT call through it. The player clears parent_ only on the Video it played, so a copy made during playback calls into a destroyed player later.

verdicts.note: Severity medium unchanged; the reproduction (member-order destruction) still triggers via ~VideoPlayer.
